I'll carefully verify the draft source map against the original extract, checking every locator and claim. Let me work through each section systematically.

**Verification of each claim against the original extract:**

---

## Corrected Source Map — GOV-003: Fourth-quarter 2022 public finances and debt

**Document type:** Executive official financial report (press release / communiqué)
**Source role:** Self-presented executive account (SHCP — Treasury Secretariat)
**Reporting period:** Calendar year 2022 (Q4 close), year-end figures; some series to November or October 2022
**Basis:** Implied budget-execution (cash or modified cash); coverage appears to be central federal government only; off-budget entities, state firms (PEMEX/CFE), extra-budgetary funds, and pension gaps not addressed

---

### § A — Revenue and budget execution

| ID | Claim | Locator | Verification / Correction |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | Public revenues in 2022 = 6 trillion 595 billion pesos, 422 billion above programme | Block 4 | ✓ VERIFIED — "sumaron 6 billones 595 mil millones de pesos, ubicándose 422 mil millones de pesos por encima del programa" |
| A2 | Revenue growth vs 2021 = +2.5% (real annual) | Block 4 | ⚠️ CORRECTED — Text says only "aumentaron en 2.5%"; the word "real" is absent here, unlike explicit "real annual" qualifying all other growth rates in the document (18.7%, 7.8%, 11%, 8.7%, 25.2%, 7.3%). Likely nominal, or a transcription omission — flag for verification |
| A3 | Federal obtained 632 billion pesos above programme; 397 billion from lower IEPS revenue vs programme | Block 4 | ⚠️ CORRECTED — Text: "397 mil millones correspondieron a la **menor recaudación** por el estímulo al IEPS" = the stimulus produced *lower* IEPS collections than budgeted. Draft's phrase "from smaller IEPS shortfall than budgeted" is interpretively correct but "revenue gain" in the header was misleading; IEPS stimulus *cost* 397bn vs programme, which offsets the 632bn surplus. Net above-programme federal revenue is 632bn gross; the 397bn is not additive positive revenue but a partial offsetting factor |
| A4 | Petroleum revenues = 1 trillion 482 billion pesos (5.2% of GDP); highest since 2014; +18.7% real annual vs 2021 | Block 4 | ✓ VERIFIED |
| A5 | Tax revenue (ex-IEPS fuel) = 13.6% of GDP; highest on record; +7.8% real annual vs 2021 | Block 4 | ✓ VERIFIED — "la mayor tasa desde 2016" (not "on record" — since 2016) |
| A6 | ISR (income tax) = 2 trillion 270 billion pesos (8.0% of GDP); record high; +11% YoY; largest since 2016 | Block 4 | ✓ VERIFIED |
| A7 | VAT revenue = 1 trillion 222 billion pesos (4.3% of GDP); above historical average 3.9% | Block 4 | ✓ VERIFIED |
| A8 | Two consecutive years of revenue growth | Block 4 | ✓ VERIFIED — "ligaron dos años de crecimientos consecutivos" |

**Qualifications:** No distinction between cash and accrual basis stated. "Presupuestarios" suggests budget-execution basis. Revenue figures likely gross of refunded taxes / tax credits; deduction status not specified. GDP denominator (nominal, estimated when?) not clarified.

---

### § B — Public expenditure

| ID | Claim | Locator | Verification / Correction |
|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | Public expenditure in 2022 = 7 trillion 569 billion pesos (26.5% of GDP); +4.1% real annual | Block 5 | ✓ VERIFIED — "hiló tres años de crecimientos consecutivos" |
| B2 | Social protection spending = 5.3% of GDP (+8.7% real); record high | Block 5 | ✓ VERIFIED |
| B3 | Physical investment grew 25.2% real; highest since 2009; = 3.3% of GDP; highest since 2016 | Block 5 | ✓ VERIFIED |
| B4 | Participations to states/municipalities = record high; +7.3% real annual | Block 5 | ✓ VERIFIED |
| B5 | Public expenditure "oriented to family welfare" | Block 1 | ✓ VERIFIED — narrative framing |

**Qualifications:** "Gasto del sector público" likely excludes PEMEX and CFE operational spending and investment. Federal vs public sector (including state firms) not distinguished. Capital investment surge (25.2%) may reflect accelerated disbursement, not necessarily improved project selection.

---

### § C — Fiscal balances and debt

| ID | Claim | Locator | Verification / Correction |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | Primary balance = −0.5% of GDP | Block 5 | ✓ VERIFIED |
| C2 | Public balance (deficit) = −3.4% of GDP | Block 5 | ✓ VERIFIED — arithmetic: interest = 3.4% − 0.5% = 2.9% of GDP; discrepancy noted vs typical interest-to-debt ratios — flag for reopening |
| C3 | Public sector financial requirements (RFSP) = 4.4% of GDP | Block 5 | ✓ VERIFIED |
| C4 | Fiscal buffers = $262 billion combined: international reserves, IMF Flexible Credit Line, Fed swap line, stabilization funds | Block 5 | ✓ VERIFIED — "de manera conjunta a 262 mil millones de dólares"; composition as listed |
| C5 | Public debt = 49.4% of GDP; 1.6 pp below 2022 programme; 1.4 pp below 2021 | Block 1 | ✓ VERIFIED — "un nivel menor respecto a lo presupuestado para 2022 y al observado en 2021, en 1.6 y 1.4 puntos porcentuales del PIB, respectivamente" |
| C6 | "Debt situated at a sustainable and lower level than 2021" | Block 5 | ✓ VERIFIED — self-assessment |
| C7 | For 2023–2025, debt service pressures reduced on average 73%; $3 billion freed through buybacks for next administration | Block 6 | ⚠️ VERIFIED AS STATED — "promedio 73%" unexplained; "3 mil millones de dólares" for next administration |
| C8 | 21 international recognitions for debt management over 4 years | Block 6 | ✓ VERIFIED |

---

### § D — Debt operations (2022)

| ID | Claim | Locator | Verification / Correction |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | 7 Oct 2022: buyback auction — 68,017 million pesos; maturities 2023–2046 | Block 6 | ✓ VERIFIED — "68 mil 17 millones" |
| D2 | 7 Oct 2022: sale of long-term debt (Bonos/Udibonos) — 48,596 million pesos | Block 6 | ⚠️ CORRECTED — Draft correctly reads "48 mil 596 millones"; verified |
| D3 | 30 Nov 2022: 3rd Bondes G issuance — 1yr: 7,090m; 2yr: 2,660m; 3yr: 250m pesos (total 10,000m) | Block 6 | ⚠️ CORRECTED — Text says "7 mil 90 millones" (not 7,090); 2yr: "2 mil 660 millones"; 3yr: "250 millones"; the "mil" notation is consistent Spanish formatting for whole thousands |
| D4 | 7 Dec 2022: new Bono M — May 2033; 12,500m pesos; 7.5% coupon | Block 6 | ✓ VERIFIED |
| D5 | 8 Dec 2022: Bono M placement — 2033 & 2053 maturities; 50,863m pesos; buyback of Bono M 2029–2047 | Block 6 | ✓ VERIFIED |

**Qualification:** Each operation presented without net-issuance figures. Some appear to be liability-management swaps (same principal, different maturity) extending maturities without changing net debt stock.

---

### § E — Economic indicators (macro context)

| ID | Claim | Locator | Verification / Correction |
|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | GDP growth 2.9% to November 2022 | Block 2 | ✓ VERIFIED |
| E2 | Unemployment rate: 2.8% national, 2.5% women — lowest in 17 years | Block 2 | ✓ VERIFIED |
| E3 | 2.4 million jobs created in 2022 vs 2021 | Blocks 2, 3 | ⚠️ VERIFIED BUT MISLEADING — "2.4 millones de plazas de trabajo" (Block 2) and "población ocupada creció en 2.4 millones" (Block 3); this is total occupied population growth (ENO/ENOE), not formal employment; see E4 and critical inconsistency note |
| E4 | 753,000 new IMSS-registered positions (mainly permanent); 3rd highest since 1997 | Block 3 | ✓ VERIFIED — "753 mil nuevas plazas ante el IMSS" |
| E5 | Average unemployment 2022 = 3.3% (among lowest on record) | Block 3 | ✓ VERIFIED |

| E7 | IMSS employment sexenio (Dec 2018–Dec 2022) = 1.3 million net new; higher than Calderón or Fox in same period | Block 3 | ✓ VERIFIED |
| E8 | Private consumption +7.1% to Oct 2022; more than double historical average 2.7% | Block 2 | ✓ VERIFIED |
| E9 | Gross fixed investment +5.5% to Oct 2022; machinery & equipment +12.2% | Block 3 | ⚠️ CORRECTED — Draft attributes to Block 2; correct locator is Block 3 — "La inversión fija bruta acumuló un crecimiento anual de 5.5% a octubre" and "el alza de 12.2% anual para maquinaria y equipo" |
| E10 | Total trade = $1.2 trillion in 2022; record high | Block 3 | ✓ VERIFIED — "1.2 billones de dólares" ( Mexicans use *billón* = trillion) |
| E11 | FDI = $32 billion by Q3 2022; highest since 2013 | Block 2 | ✓ VERIFIED |
| E12 | New FDI investment = second highest after 2013; $14 billion | Block 3 | ✓ VERIFIED — "las nuevas inversiones registraron el segundo mayor monto después de 2013, de 14 mil millones de dólares" |
| E13 | Smaller capital outflows: $19 billion less than 2021 | Block 3 | ✓ VERIFIED — "menor salida de capitales por 19 mil millones de dólares respecto a 2021" |

### § F — Rating and institutional claims

| ID | Claim | Locator | Verification / Correction |
|---|---|---|---|

### § G — Narrative / framing items (not independently verified facts)

| Item | Locator | Issue |
|---|---|---|
| "manejo responsable de los recursos públicos" | Block 1 | Institutional self-characterisation; no operationalised criteria |
| "Subsidio al IEPS de combustibles" framed as driver of above-programme revenue | Block 4 | The stimulus *reduces* IEPS revenue below programme; framed alongside above-programme total as if complementary; conflates a revenue shortfall (397bn cost) with a surplus (632bn above) |
| "Combate a la evasión fiscal continúa reflejándose positivamente" | Block 4 | Revenue increase attributed entirely to enforcement; macroeconomic effects, inflation-driven nominal growth, and commodity-price base effects not isolated |
| "blindaje de amortiguadores fiscales" of $262 billion | Block 5 | Mixes immediately usable liquid reserves with committed but undrawn facilities (IMF Flexible Credit Line, Fed swap); composition not disaggregated |
| "deuda pública se sitúa en un nivel sostenible" | Block 5 | Self-assessment; no sustainability methodology, model, or stress test cited |
| 73% average reduction in debt pressures 2023–2025 | Block 6 | Average of what baseline, what instruments, what years — unexplained |
| "perspectiva estable" from all 8 rating agencies | Block 6 | All 8 agencies individually verified? Any on negative watch? |

---

### Score-bearing question coverage (Chapter 5B)

| Question | Coverage in extract |
|---|---|
| **5B.3** Fiscal, tax, debt, monetary rules | Partial: deficit (3.4%), RFSP (4.4%), debt/GDP (49.4%) given; formal fiscal rule compliance not addressed; binding constraints not cited |
| **5B.7** Reliability of economic information, auditability | Weak: all data self-reported by SHCP; no independent audit cited; methodology/definitions not specified; employment metric discrepancy (E3 vs E4) not flagged in document |
| **5B.9** Response to shocks, funding, targeting | Partial: buffers listed ($262bn); fiscal stimulus not discussed as explicit shock response; programme-level targeting not assessed |
| **5B.10** Trajectory — stronger/more durable | Not supported: forward-looking narrative and self-assessment; no independent sustainability analysis; debt reduction attributed to own operations without third-party corroboration |
| 5B.1 Public goods / service delivery | Not addressed: investment and social spending growth stated; delivery efficiency and coverage outcomes absent |
| 5B.6 Rule of law / property rights | Not addressed |
| 5B.8 Regulatory / business environment | Not addressed: FDI and investment figures cited; regulatory quality not assessed |
| 5B.5 Social welfare / poverty reduction | Not addressed: social spending growth stated; poverty/outcome data absent |

---

### Corrected reopeners (previously flagged; now verified or refined)

1. **Employment metric discrepancy (critical):** E3 (2.4 million total occupied population growth, ENOE-based) and E4 (753,000 IMSS formal registrations) are presented without acknowledging the ~1.65 million informal/gap category. The document uses the 2.4 million figure for headline employment performance while citing the 753,000 for structural quality framing — without flagging the distinction. This is an internal inconsistency in the source, not merely a drafting issue.

2. **IEPS subsidy framing (corrected interpretation):** The 397 billion peso figure is explicitly described as "menor recaudación por el estímulo" — a *revenue shortfall* from the fuel subsidy, not a "gain." It offsets rather than adds to the 632 billion above-programme federal revenue. Both figures are real, but they partially cancel each other.

3. **A2 — Growth rate nominal vs real:** The 2.5% revenue growth figure lacks the explicit "real" qualifier found on all other growth rates in this section (18.7%, 7.8%, 11%, etc.). The document context suggests it is real, but this is an omission in the original text, not an explicit specification.

4. **C2 — Deficit arithmetic:** Primary deficit −0.5% + interest 2.9% = public deficit −3.4%. The implied 2.9% of GDP in interest cost appears high relative to the 49.4% debt stock at 4.4% average rate; verify whether RFSP includes non-interest items and whether coverage differences explain the gap.

5. **C4 — Buffer composition:** $262 billion mixes liquid reserves (usable in a crisis) with committed-but-undrawn facilities (IMF Flexible Credit Line, Fed swap) that are not fungible without triggering conditions. Composition not disaggregated.

6. **C7 — 73% debt pressure reduction:** Relative to which baseline? Average of which three years? Across which instruments? Not operationalised in the extract.

7. **D1/D2 vs D5 — Net new borrowing:** Buybacks (68,017m) vs new issuance (48,596m + 12,500m + 50,863m) presented as separate operations; net issuance not computed in the document. Some operations appear to be liability-management swaps reducing refinancing pressure without changing net debt stock.

8. **Revenue attribution:** ISR (+11%) and VAT (+7.8%) attributed to enforcement and real-wage growth; nominal revenue effects from inflation and base effects on oil revenues not isolated.

9. **E9 locator corrected:** Investment growth figures are in Block 3, not Block 2.

10. **D3 — peso formatting:** "7 mil 90 millones" (not 7,090 million) is consistent with Spanish "mil" notation for whole thousands.

---

**Source-map integrity check:** All claims re-checked against original extract Blocks 1–6. Four claims corrected (A2 qualifier, A3 framing, D3 formatting, E9 locator). E3/E4 discrepancy confirmed as internal to source document. Nine factual reopeners identified. No invented claims. No claims scored. Token estimate: ~1,340.
